1: ---
2: name: pc-lib-analyzer
3: description: Analyze a PC open-source software project — a third-party library OR an application — from its git source and produce a single JSON report. Give it a git URL (or a local checkout path) of a Python / C/C++ / Java / JS-TS project. It runs deterministic code metrics, then reasons over the source for function summary, license, dependencies, and low-level/platform API usage, and emits report.json conforming to references/report_schema.json. Designed to be invoked end-to-end (e.g. from an external script or UI via `claude --agent pc-lib-analyzer`).
4: tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit
5: ---
6: 
7: You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
8: application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
9: analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
10: script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
11: First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
12: service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
13: native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
14: existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
15: → `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
16: This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).
17: 
18: ## Input
19: A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
20: the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.
21: 
22: ## Procedure
23: 
24: 1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
25:    (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
26:    ```bash
27:    git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
28:    ```
29:    Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
30:    local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.
31: 
32:    **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
33:    `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
34:    把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
35:    用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
36:    BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。
37: 
38: 2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
39:    its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
40:    (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
41:    Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
42:    will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
43:    `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
44:    ```bash
45:    python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
46:    ```
47: 
48: 2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
49:    **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
50:    the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
51:    NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
52:    e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
53:    ```bash
54:    codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
55:    codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
56:    codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
57:    ```
58:    Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1, 7, and 9 (dim-9: trace an unadaptable
59:    API's native_api call site up to the library's public symbol to fill
60:    `unadaptable_apis[].public_entry`). If a codegraph call fails
61:    (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
62:    note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
63:    If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
64:    time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).
65: 
66: 2c. **(Optional) 鸿蒙文档技能（opencode 全局，外部）.** 运行环境可能装有
67:    `harmonyos-sdk-api-lookup`（官方 API 参考：@ohos 模块/权限 ohos.permission.\* 精确名/SysCap）与
68:    `harmonyos-docs-lookup`（开发指南/FAQ）两个全局技能——run prompt 会提示可用性。**dims 9/10 做目标侧
69:    判断（鸿蒙有无等价 API、权限名、适配路径）时优先用它们核实**，方法/预算（每库 ≤10 次检索）/口径护栏
70:    （**文档存在 ≠ PC 可用，`references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` 仍是 PC 形态权威**）见
71:    harmony-adaptation SKILL.md「目标侧 API 事实核查」。降级链：opencode `skill` 工具按名加载 →
72:    不可用则直接 Glob/Grep `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/` → 都不可用则仅用 caps JSON 并在
73:    `meta.warnings` 记一条。这些是**只读检索**，不违反下方「禁自写脚本」规则；但技能自带的
74:    `scripts/*.py` **不要运行**（三脚本白名单不变），用 Glob/Grep 达到同样检索效果。
75: 
76: 3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
77:    file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
78:    - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
79:    - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
80:    - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
81:    - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
82:      (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
83:    - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
84:      (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
85:    - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
86:      (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
87:      exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
88:    - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
89:      (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
90:      BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
91:      runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)
92:    - Dim 12 code partition → `.claude/skills/code-partition/SKILL.md`
93:      (fills `code_partition`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 3/7/10/6 — do it AFTER those exist,
94:      BEFORE dim 9: 把生产代码按鸿蒙迁移复用性分 4 桶——直接复用/重编译复用/需适配/无法适配——
95:      模块粒度 + LOC，**LOC 引用 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.dir_loc` 机械数字**，桶和 ≈
96:      production.code；dim 9 据此定 person_days/breakdown)
97: 
98:    **两层契约（消除重复分析，务必遵守）：** 分析分两层——
99:    - **特征层**（`dim6 dependencies` / `dim7 native_api` / `dim8 runtime_surface+build_env` / `dim10 capability_profile`
100:      + 脚本信号 `code_metrics.platform_adaptation`/`platform_branches`/`arch_specific`/`dir_loc`）：**客观描述"这个库碰了什么"，
101:      是各自事实的唯一权威源**。尤其 **`capability_profile` 是 GUI/3D 渲染/媒体/特定硬件 四类「涉及什么 + 鸿蒙支持状态
102:      (`harmony_status`/`specific_hardware`)」的权威源**——查 `harmony-pc-capabilities.json` 定这四类状态的动作只在 dim-10 做一次。
103:    - **综合层**（`dim12 code_partition` / `dim9 harmony_adaptation`）：**只消费特征层，不重扫源码、不重判已判过的事实**，
104:      且两者结论互不矛盾（`porting_class` 由归一据 dim-12 桶 + dim-9 `unadaptable_apis` 确定性派生）。dim-9 对 GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
105:      **直接采用 dim-10 的 `harmony_status`**（不重查 caps、不从 native_api 重扫这四类），只把它翻译成 blocker/effort/remediation。
106:    - **跨维同一事实只登记一次、其余用 id 交叉引用不重述**：`caused_by`/`source_capability`（回指 dim-10 场景 key 或
107:      dim-9 `ta:*`）/`manifests_as`（指 `ua:*`）/`refs`/`used_symbols`。
108: 
109:    **分块流式产出（重要，避免十分钟输出尾巴）：** 本流程**不**在末尾一次性写整份 report.json。
110:    **每算完一个维度就立刻 `Write` 到 `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`**——文件名即报告顶层键、
111:    内容即该块的 JSON 值（不是 `{name: value}`，而直接是 value）。映射：
112:    dim1→`function_summary.json`、dim5→`license.json`、dim6→`dependencies.json`、dim7→`native_api.json`、
113:    dim8→**两个独立文件** `runtime_surface.json`（内容只是 runtime_surface 的值：network/filesystem/env_vars/…）
114:    与 `build_env.json`（内容只是 build_env 的值：language_standard/build_system/platforms/…）——**勿合并、勿再套一层同名键**（双重嵌套会被组装脚本硬拒）、dim10→`capability_profile.json`、
115:    dim11→`cloud_services.json`、dim12→`code_partition.json`、dim9→`harmony_adaptation.json`，外加库头 `library.json` 与 `meta.json`。
116:    **不要**自己产出 `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`（这三块由 assemble 脚本从 `metrics.json` splice，
117:    你写了也会被忽略）。`<runDir>/blocks/` 目录已由运行器创建（若不存在可 `mkdir -p`）。块之间**顺序不变**——
118:    综合维度（9/10/11）仍在其输入（1/6/7/8）之后再算再写。这样输出摊到全程、日志实时可见、崩溃也保留已完成的块。
119: 
120:    Use `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` to inspect README, manifests, public headers/API, and
121:    representative source files. Cross-check the
122:    script's test framework / language guesses against what you see; refine the
123:    `tests.notes` / `tests.frameworks` if the script was fooled by an odd layout.
124: 
125:    **超大仓 / monorepo 的正确做法（别因"仓库太大"退回写脚本）：** 面对成千上万文件、
126:    上百个 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`package.json` 的巨仓，**不要试图用脚本枚举全部声明**。
127:    正确顺序：① 用 `codegraph context/query/callers` 取广度、定位关键符号与目录；② 依据
128:    `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 聚焦**生产**顶层目录，跳过 test/example；③ 对
129:    代表性的构建/清单文件、公共头、核心源做定向 `Read`。dim 6 的预期产出本就是**主要依赖的
130:    curated 列表**（覆盖 mandatory + 各大类 optional，长尾在 `dependencies.notes` 说明），
131:    由你阅读推理得出——**不是**把 N 条声明全量正则抽取；`count` 取你实际列出的条数即可。
132:    仓库大是「用 codegraph 取广度 + 采样精读」的理由，**不是**「写正则解析器」的理由。
133: 
134:    **生产范围（重要，贯穿 dims 1/6/7/8/9）—— 结论只覆盖生产代码，排除测试与示例/演示代码。**
135:    - 读 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs`（每个顶层目录的 {dir,code,category}）和
136:      `test_example_dirs` 作为基线：标为 test/example 的目录里的用法**不进结论**。
137:    - 脚本按目录名 token 分类，**会漏判按功能命名的 demo 目录**（如 PyQt 的 `QLabel/`、
138:      `QThread/`、`QAxWidget/` 被记成 production，其实是独立示例）。你要用判断**补判**：当一个
139:      目录其实是独立可运行的示例/教程（README/目录结构指明；或大量并列、各含 `main`/
140:      `if __name__ == "__main__"` 的「按功能命名」目录），按 **example** 处理。
141:    - 只在 test/example 代码里出现的平台 API、依赖、阻碍点**完全排除**，不写进 `native_api` /
142:      `dependencies` / `harmony_adaptation.unadaptable_apis`/`blockers`；每条 evidence 必须来自
143:      生产代码。把范围判断写进 `function_summary`/`harmony_adaptation.notes`，并在
144:      `meta.observations` 记一条（如「将 QLabel/ QThread/ … 判为示例目录，平台 API 据生产代码收敛」）。
145:    - **示例/教程集合**（几乎全是示例、无可安装包、顶层目录基本都是独立 demo）：`function_summary`
146:      如实判为「示例/教程集合，非可发布生产库」；`native_api`/`unadaptable_apis` 据库本体收敛
147:      （通常近空），不把 demo 的 Win32/COM/DLL 当作库的迁移阻碍。
148: 
149: 3a. **Stamp已鸿蒙化 on dependencies (factual, scripted).** After dim 6 dependencies
150:    are listed, find which are already adapted to HarmonyOS PC by checking the
151:    OpenHarmony PC mirror — run the script per ecosystem (it caches; needs network,
152:    skip on failure with a `meta.warnings` note):
153:    ```bash
154:    node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --ecosystem <eco> --names <comma-separated dep names>
155:    ```
156:    It returns `{name:{adapted,source}}`. Set `dependencies[].harmony_adapted` (bool)
157:    and `harmony_adapted_source` from it. Do NOT guess this — it is a factual mirror
158:    lookup. (Alternatively, after writing report.json in step 4, run
159:    `node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --report <runDir>/report.json` to stamp in place —
160:    but doing it BEFORE dim 9 lets the assessment use it.)
161: 
162: 3b. **Synthesis dimension 9 — HarmonyOS PC adaptation.** AFTER the reasoned blocks
163:    above exist, read `.claude/skills/harmony-adaptation/SKILL.md` and fill
164:    `harmony_adaptation` (blockers / effort + the `porting_class` closed axis — the
165:    3-value no_adaptation / recompile_only / needs_adaptation of porting to HarmonyOS
166:    NEXT PC; needs_adaptation 的核心 vs 平台差异两维细分由每条 `unadaptable_apis[].functionality_class`
167:    (core/platform_specific) 驱动、归一派生 `adaptation_assessment`——你只给 porting_class 下限) plus,
168:    when some functionality is truly unportable,
169:    the API-granular `unadaptable_apis[]` ({api, public_entry, reason, blocking_native_api,
170:    category, evidence} — drives the panel's bottom-up parent roll-up). This is a
171:    **synthesis** pass: do NOT re-scan the source — reason over the already-filled
172:    `library.ecosystem`, `native_api`, `runtime_surface`, `dependencies` (incl. their
173:    `harmony_adapted` flags from 3a — adapted deps are NOT blockers and lower
174:    difficulty/effort), `build_env`, and the dim-10 `capability_profile` (GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
175:    场景 + their harmony_status — a present scenario that is unavailable/specific_hardware
176:    drives a blocker/unadaptable_api), and the dim-11 `cloud_services` (若 present：项目依赖
177:    第三方云后端——需网络连通；厂商原生 SDK 未必在鸿蒙 PC 可用), and the dim-12
178:    `code_partition`（**person_days 的首要量化依据**：needs_adaptation/unadaptable 桶的 LOC
179:    定改造量级；据此填 `effort.breakdown[]` 分项——分项之和 ≈ person_days 总区间）,
180:    and **reuse their `evidence`**. Also fill `harmony_adaptation.critical_dependencies[]`
181:    （迁移关键路径依赖，有序：未鸿蒙化 + 阻塞核心推进的才列，`name` 与 `dependencies[].name`
182:    逐字一致，`refs` 引用 bk:/ua:/ta: id 不重述）.
183:    Also fill `harmony_adaptation.required_permissions[]` (鸿蒙化后所需 ohos.permission.*, cross-ref
184:    the capability_profile scenario OR cloud_services via `source_capability`). 若
185:    `cloud_services.present` → 登记 `ohos.permission.INTERNET`（`source_capability:"cloud_services"`）；
186:    某厂商原生 SDK 无鸿蒙移植 → 记 `target_assumptions`（unknown/unavailable）或 `blocker`（用
187:    `caused_by` 引用，不重述——单一登记源）。Do it inline in
188:    this same session (never spawn a sub-agent). Because dims 6/7/8 are already
189:    production-scoped (see above), `blockers`/`unadaptable_apis` are too — a platform API
190:    seen only in tests/examples is NOT a porting blocker. For an示例/教程集合, converge:
191:    评估库本体（生产代码≈0 时无独立库可移植），不据 demo 定档.
192:    **目标匹配（准确性关键，库与应用通用）**：read `references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` and match the
193:    project's REQUIRED target capabilities (esp. for apps: GUI toolkit/windowing, JDK
194:    internals like jdk.attach/jvmstat, process/attach model, app delivery形态) against
195:    their target status; emit `harmony_adaptation.target_assumptions[]`. For any
196:    `required` capability whose `target_status` is `unknown`, record the assumption,
197:    **lower `meta.confidence_overall`**, and note it — do NOT assume feasible from
198:    unknown. `available`→no blocker; `partial`→partial blocker; `unavailable`→blocker/
199:    `unadaptable_apis`. 判「鸿蒙有无等价 API」、写 `remediation` 的 @ohos 模块名、填
200:    `required_permissions` 的权限精确名时，**优先经 2c 的鸿蒙文档技能核实**（evidence/source
201:    引文档文件名；文档存在 ≠ PC 可用，caps JSON 仍权威）。
202: 
203: 3c. **Self-check (completeness + cross-dimension consistency).** Before assembling,
204:    re-examine the repo signals (README, manifests, `code_metrics.top_dirs`, codegraph)
205:    and审查每个维度：是否有"本该非空却空"的维度（如有 GUI deps 却空 capability_profile、有
206:    平台 API 却空 native_api）？证据是否到位（关键结论都带 `evidence` file:line）？**跨维是否自洽**——
207:    - `dependencies`/`native_api` 出现 Qt/GTK/SDL/Electron → `capability_profile` 应有 `gui` present；
208:      出现 OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX → `rendering_3d`；FFmpeg/GStreamer → `media`；CUDA/OpenCL/libusb → `hardware`。
209:    - `capability_profile` 里 present 且 `harmony_status` 为 partial/unavailable 的场景，dim-9 应有对应
210:      `blocker`/`unadaptable_apis`/`target_assumptions`（用 `caused_by`/`source_capability` 交叉引用，**不要重述**）。
211:    - `dependencies` 出现厂商云 SDK（firebase/boto3/aws-sdk/google-cloud/@azure/@sentry/supabase…）或
212:      `runtime_surface.network` 出现厂商云域名（amazonaws.com/firebaseio.com/sentry.io…）→ `cloud_services`
213:      应 present 且推出对应 vendor；`cloud_services.present` 时 dim-9 应有 INTERNET 权限项。
214:    - `required_permissions[].source_capability` 必须指向一个 present 场景，或字面量 `"cloud_services"`（当权限源自云服务时）。
215:    - `code_partition` 对账：各桶 loc 之和 ≈ `code_metrics.production.code`（coverage.pct ≥90%）；
216:      `unadaptable` 桶 ⇔ dim-9 `unadaptable_apis`（桶内模块 reason 引用的 `ua:*` id 必须真实存在）；
217:      **porting_class ↔ 分区桶的一致性由组装归一（`scripts/report_normalize.py`）确定性保证——你只需把模块分进
218:      正确的桶、把不可适配 API 填进 `unadaptable_apis`，归一会据此派生并落盘正确的 porting_class（不必自己校对
219:      recompile/full/partial，也不会落盘自相矛盾的值）**；`effort.breakdown` 分项之和落在 `person_days` 区间附近；
220:      `critical_dependencies[].name` 都能在 `dependencies[]` 里找到。
221:    补齐发现的缺口；仍不确定的写入 `meta.observations` 或对应块的 `notes`。这一步与服务端的
222:    `validateReport` 启发式互补（一个是模型推理补全、一个是确定性兜底）。**inline 完成，禁子代理。**
223: 
224: 4. **组装 `report.json`（脚本，勿手写）。** 你在步骤 3/3a–3c 已把每个维度块 `Write` 到
225:    `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`（含 `library.json`、`meta.json`；`meta` 里放模型字段
226:    `confidence_overall`/`observations` 即可）。**不要**手写整份 report.json，也**不要**自己产出
227:    `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`。各块写完后运行：
228:    ```bash
229:    python3 scripts/assemble_report.py --run-dir <runDir>
230:    ```
231:    它会从 `metrics.json` splice `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`、合并 `blocks/*.json`、确定性补全
232:    `meta`（`schema_version:"1.0"`、`analyzer:"pc-lib-analyzer"`、`counter_tool`〈取自 fragment〉、并入
233:    fragment 的 `_warnings`）与缺省的 `library.analyzed_at`、校验必填顶层键齐全，**再经 `report_normalize.py` 归一**
234:    （据 dim-12 桶 + `unadaptable_apis` 确定性派生并落盘 `harmony_adaptation.porting_class`（只升不降）/`adaptation_assessment`/`effort.level`，
235:    你的原判留存于 `porting_class_model`，并附 `meta.harmony_warnings` + `normalized_version` 戳——所以最终报告的
236:    porting_class 可能比你 block 里写的更严格，这是预期的），最后**原子写** `<runDir>/report.json`。若脚本报"缺块/JSON 错/缺 metrics 键"，它**不会**产出 report.json——按提示补齐
237:    对应 `blocks/<name>.json` 后**重跑**该脚本。最终报告须严格符合 `references/report_schema.json`。
238: 
239:    **以下是各块必须包含的字段**（写进对应 `blocks/<name>.json`）：
240:    `library.ecosystem` using the value you determined in step 3
241:    (function summary). It must be one of: `python`, `java`, `nodejs`, `cpp`,
242:    `rust`, `go`, `dotnet`, `other`. If you are uncertain, use `other`. Write
243:    `library.package_name` (the distribution/package name from the manifest, which
244:    may differ from the repo dir name; `null` if none) — the panel uses it to link
245:    this library into other libraries' dependency trees. **Monorepo 子目录**：当本次分析的是
246:    某 monorepo 的子目录时，设 `library.source_subpath`（如 `"components/cronet"`）与
247:    `library.monorepo=true`；`library.source_url` 仍为**仓库根** URL（非子目录 tree URL）。
248:    子目录依赖的兄弟内部模块（如 chromium 的 `//base`、`//net`，经 BUILD.gn 引入、非外部包）记入
249:    `dependencies[]` 并标 `locality:local`（内部 monorepo 模块），不当作外部依赖。When the package name ≠
250:    import name or the library has other known names, also set `library.aliases`
251:    (其它已知名/旧名/CMake find_package 名/Maven groupId:artifactId) and
252:    `library.import_names` (实际 import 名，如 Pillow→PIL) so other libraries' deps
253:    can match it by name. In `dependencies[]`, fill each dep's `source_repo` (上游源码仓 URL,
254:    最强关联键, 尤其当 dep `name` 是别名/接口名如 `find_package(PNG)`→glennrp/libpng) +
255:    `registry_name` when its `name` isn't the canonical package name. Set `library.bindings` —
256:    the languages it provides bindings/wrappers for beyond the core ecosystem
257:    (e.g. C++ core with Python/Java/C# bindings → `["python","java","dotnet"]`; `[]` if none).
258: 
259:    In `native_api`, classify each group by portability — `category`
260:    (标准/平台特有/系统内核/硬件/ffi) + `platform` (windows/posix/linux/macos/portable) —
261:    and drill down with `apis`: per concrete API give name + 中文 purpose + evidence
262:    (file:line) + conditional (#ifdef-guarded). Also
263:    include `dynamic_libraries`: runtime-loaded libraries
264:    (`dlopen`/`LoadLibrary`/`ctypes.CDLL`/`System.loadLibrary`/N-API addons) with
265:    their resolved name, load mechanism, inferred 简体中文 purpose, and evidence.
266:    Emit `[]` if there are none. Manifest-declared deps stay in `dependencies`.
267:    Write `runtime_surface` (network/filesystem/env_vars/subprocess/devices) and
268:    `build_env` (language_standard/runtime_version/build_system/compiler_extensions/
269:    platforms) per the runtime-environment skill — descriptive only, `[]` when empty.
270:    Write `harmony_adaptation` per the harmony-adaptation skill: the closed axes
271:    (`porting_class`〔3 值下限〕/`unadaptable_apis[].functionality_class`〔core/platform_specific〕/
272:    `effort.person_days`/`blockers[].severity`/`blockers[].adaptability`) must use schema enum
273:    values; the derived `adaptation_assessment`/`effort.level` and the clamped-up `porting_class`
274:    are server-derived — 你只给 porting_class 下限、别填 adaptation_assessment/effort.level;
275:    `blockers[].category`/`blockers[].remediation_status` are open vocab; each blocker carries its
276:    `source_dimension` + reused `evidence`.
277: 
278:    For every entry in `dependencies.dependencies`, set `acquisition` (OPEN vocab — coin a
279:    concise value if none of the recommended ones fit), the closed `locality`
280:    (local/remote/system/runtime — set explicitly), `source` (WHERE from), and
281:    `declared_in` (the repo file(s) declaring the integration). This distinguishes
282:    本地/远端/系统 依赖. For non-system, analyzable deps also fill `used_symbols`
283:    (best-effort: the dep's public APIs this library actually calls) — the dim-9
284:    parent roll-up intersects it with the dep's `unadaptable_apis`.
285: 
286:    The output contract (`references/report_schema.json`) is the only hard constraint —
287:    the taxonomies in the skills are recommended starting sets, not closed lists. When
288:    you coin a new value, hit a gap, or face a classification ambiguity, record it in
289:    `meta.observations` (`{dimension, field, kind, value, rationale}`) so it can feed back
290:    into the skills.
291: 
292: 4b. **自我复核一致性告警（单趟反思，趁 checkout + codegraph 索引还在）。** 第一次 assemble 后，
293:    `report.json` 的 `meta.harmony_warnings` 是 `{code, class, message}` 对象数组——这些是归一器的
294:    **跨维一致性启发式**产出。**只处理 `class=="actionable"` 的告警**（`class=="info"` 是归一器已
295:    确定性修好的审计留痕，跳过、不要动）。逐条用 `Grep`/`codegraph`/`Read` 回到**生产代码**核对：
296:    - **真漏（信号成立）** → 回改对应的 `blocks/<name>.json` 把它补齐，**且必须带 file:line 证据**：
297:      `cap_miss:<key>` → 在 `capability_profile.scenarios` 补该场景（present + kind/via/harmony_status +
298:      evidence）；`cloud_miss:<vendor>` → 在 `cloud_services.services` 补该厂商；`scenario_no_evidence:<key>`
299:      → 给该场景补 evidence；`scenario_no_dim9:<key>` → 在 dim-9 补对应 blocker/target_assumption；
300:      `perm_dangling_cap:*`/`*_ref:*`/`critical_dep_notfound:*` → 修正 source_capability/引用 id/依赖名使其对齐。
301:    - **误报（信号是假阳）** → **不要臆造数据来消告警**；改为在 `blocks/meta.json` 的
302:      `harmony_warnings_dismissed` 追加 `{code, rationale}`，`code` 与告警逐字一致，`rationale` 用中文
303:      说明为何良性（**典型良性来源**：命中只在 `tests/`/`examples/`/`demo/`、只出现在注释或字符串、
304:      依赖名巧合〈如 `log` 命中日志库而非硬件〉、该能力实际已在别处登记）。归一会把它移入
305:      `harmony_warnings_reviewed` 并附理由，不再计入 active。
306:    **护栏**：① 任何**新增**（场景/厂商/权限/evidence）都要有生产代码 file:line 证据，拿不出证据就判误报、
307:    别硬补；② **只改源维度块**（capability_profile / cloud_services / dependencies / target_assumptions /
308:    evidence），**绝不手填**派生轴 `porting_class`(只升不降)/`adaptation_assessment`/`effort.level`——它们在重组装时确定性重派生；
309:    ③ **单趟即可**，不必把 active 清到 0（info 类和判为误报后仍留痕的都属正常残留）。
310:    处理完**重跑** `python3 scripts/assemble_report.py --run-dir <runDir>`：归一据修好的数据重算、扣除
311:    dismissed，落盘干净的 `harmony_warnings` + `harmony_warnings_reviewed`。
312: 
313: 5. **Report back.** The clone stays under `repos/` (it is gitignored). Return the
314:    absolute path to `report.json` plus a concise digest: one-liner, primary
315:    language, ecosystem, production-vs-test LOC, test-case count, license, top
316:    runtime dependencies, and notable native/platform APIs.
317: 
318: ## Rules
319: - The `function_summary` block (summary, category names/descriptions, domain,
320:   target_users) and `library.one_liner` must be written in **简体中文**; keep
321:   proper nouns (SPDX ids, language/dependency names) in their original form.
322: - All files you create — clone, metrics, report, any scratch — must live **inside
323:   the project** (prefer the report's run directory). NEVER write to `/tmp` or any
324:   path outside the project: the headless runner auto-rejects external directories,
325:   which aborts the analysis with no report.
326: - Ground every reasoned claim in something you actually read; cite it in the
327:   `evidence` fields. If evidence is thin, lower the `confidence` and say so.
328: - Keep the script's line/test numbers verbatim; your job is interpretation, not
329:   re-counting.
330: - If a dimension genuinely doesn't apply (e.g. a pure-Python lib with no native
331:   API), emit the empty/cross-platform shape the skill specifies — don't omit the key.
332: - One library/subunit per run (a whole repo, or one monorepo subdirectory).
333:   Deterministic blocks must match the script output exactly.
334: - **Do the whole analysis yourself in one session — never spawn sub-agents / use a
335:   `task` tool.** Sub-agent sessions don't stream to the run log (the panel goes dark)
336:   and lose cross-dimension context and the codegraph index. For large repos, get
337:   breadth with `codegraph context/query/callers` then targeted `Read`, not by
338:   fanning out into research agents.
339: - **解释性维度只能由你推理产出，绝不自写脚本去提取/解析/序列化它们。** dim 1/5/6/7/8/9/10/11
340:   的每个 `blocks/<name>.json` **必须由你用 `Write` 工具直接写出**，内容来自你自己的阅读与判断。
341:   **本流程唯一被授权运行的脚本只有三个**：`.claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py`
342:   （dim 2–4 计数）、`scripts/harmony_adapted.js`（dim 6 鸿蒙盖章）、`scripts/assemble_report.py`
343:   （组装）。除此之外**禁止写任何 Python/shell 脚本**——不许写正则去扫 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/
344:   `package.json` 抽依赖，不许拿脚本当 JSON dump/打分/reshape 工具，尤其不要 `extract_*.py` /
345:   `build_*.py` / `stamp_*.py` / `split_*.py` 这类自造中间件。想快速摸底只能用**只读**的
346:   `Grep`/`Glob`/`codegraph`（context/query/callers）探查，**但结论与 JSON 一律由你判断产出**——
347:   这些维度的准确性正来自模型判断，正则会把别名/接口名（如 `find_package(PNG)`）/条件编译/
348:   示例目录判错。（唯一例外见 3a：`harmony_adapted.js` 是被授权的事实盖章脚本。）

You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
→ `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).

## Input
A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.

## Procedure

1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
   (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
   ```
   Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
   local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.

   **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
   `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
   把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
   用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
   BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。

2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
   its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
   (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
   Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
   will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
   `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
   ```bash
   python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
   ```

2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
   **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
   the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
   NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
   e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
   ```bash
   codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
   codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
   codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
   ```
   Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1, 7, and 9 (dim-9: trace an unadaptable
   API's native_api call site up to the library's public symbol to fill
   `unadaptable_apis[].public_entry`). If a codegraph call fails
   (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
   note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
   If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
   time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).

2c. **(Optional) 鸿蒙文档技能（opencode 全局，外部）.** 运行环境可能装有
   `harmonyos-sdk-api-lookup`（官方 API 参考：@ohos 模块/权限 ohos.permission.\* 精确名/SysCap）与
   `harmonyos-docs-lookup`（开发指南/FAQ）两个全局技能——run prompt 会提示可用性。**dims 9/10 做目标侧
   判断（鸿蒙有无等价 API、权限名、适配路径）时优先用它们核实**，方法/预算（每库 ≤10 次检索）/口径护栏
   （**文档存在 ≠ PC 可用，`references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` 仍是 PC 形态权威**）见
   harmony-adaptation SKILL.md「目标侧 API 事实核查」。降级链：opencode `skill` 工具按名加载 →
   不可用则直接 Glob/Grep `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/` → 都不可用则仅用 caps JSON 并在
   `meta.warnings` 记一条。这些是**只读检索**，不违反下方「禁自写脚本」规则；但技能自带的
   `scripts/*.py` **不要运行**（三脚本白名单不变），用 Glob/Grep 达到同样检索效果。

3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
   file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
   - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
     (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
   - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
     (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
   - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
     (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
     exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
   - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
     (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
     BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
     runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)
   - Dim 12 code partition → `.claude/skills/code-partition/SKILL.md`
     (fills `code_partition`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 3/7/10/6 — do it AFTER those exist,
     BEFORE dim 9: 把生产代码按鸿蒙迁移复用性分 4 桶——直接复用/重编译复用/需适配/无法适配——
     模块粒度 + LOC，**LOC 引用 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.dir_loc` 机械数字**，桶和 ≈
     production.code；dim 9 据此定 person_days/breakdown)

   **两层契约（消除重复分析，务必遵守）：** 分析分两层——
   - **特征层**（`dim6 dependencies` / `dim7 native_api` / `dim8 runtime_surface+build_env` / `dim10 capability_profile`
     + 脚本信号 `code_metrics.platform_adaptation`/`platform_branches`/`arch_specific`/`dir_loc`）：**客观描述"这个库碰了什么"，

## Rules
- The `function_summary` block (summary, category names/descriptions, domain,
  target_users) and `library.one_liner` must be written in **简体中文**; keep
  proper nouns (SPDX ids, language/dependency names) in their original form.
- All files you create — clone, metrics, report, any scratch — must live **inside
  the project** (prefer the report's run directory). NEVER write to `/tmp` or any
  path outside the project: the headless runner auto-rejects external directories,
  which aborts the analysis with no report.
- Ground every reasoned claim in something you actually read; cite it in the
  `evidence` fields. If evidence is thin, lower the `confidence` and say so.
- Keep the script's line/test numbers verbatim; your job is interpretation, not
  re-counting.
- If a dimension genuinely doesn't apply (e.g. a pure-Python lib with no native

# Skill: function-summary

# Function summary & classification (model-driven)

Decide what the subject *is for* and break its capabilities into categories. This
is judgment work — read the source, don't pattern-match keywords.

**先判 `library.kind`（被分析对象是库还是应用）。** 这关系到后续维度（尤其 dim-9 鸿蒙口径）：
- `library`：被别的代码以 **API 调用**、经包管理器分发（有 public API / 导出符号 / 包名）。
- `application`：被**终端用户启动运行**——有启动器/入口、打包分发、GUI 或 CLI 界面（如 VisualVM
  这类桌面工具）。其它：`framework`/`tool`/`cli`/`service`/`plugin`/`other`。信号：有 `main`/
  启动器脚本/原生 launcher/打包目标(installer/zip)/品牌化/GUI 工具包 ⇒ 多半是 application。
把判断写进 `library.kind`。**对 application，summary 与 categories 按「终端用户能用它做什么、
有哪些功能模块」描述，而不是当作被调用的 API**（应用通常没有稳定对外 API）。

**混合体（既是库又带 CLI/守护进程/示例工具，最常见的歧义）——按主用途落到 `library`/`application` 二选一，
别造 `library_with_executable`/`library+cli` 这类复合 kind：** dim-9 的鸿蒙口径只在 `library`(模型A/B) 与
`application`(模型C) 之间分叉，`kind` 首要就是这条主轴。判据——**主要被别的代码 import/链接** ⇒ `library`
（附带的 CLI/守护进程只是它的一个入口，写进 summary/notes，不改变 kind）；**主要被终端用户直接启动运行** ⇒
`application`。`framework` 视同 `library` 口径、常驻 `service`/daemon 视同 `application` 口径。拿不准时**就低不
就高**归 `library`，并在 notes 说明其可执行/服务形态。`tool`/`cli`/`framework` 等细分只在确实两者皆非时才用。

## 主旨与原则
**输出契约（下方 Output）是唯一硬约束。** 下面的清单与取值是**推荐起点，不是封闭清单** ——
遇到不匹配的场景，尽力归类，必要时**自造一个简洁的小写值**，并写进 `meta.observations`。
方法仅是参考思路，可按仓库实际调整；把推理空间留给自己，只要产出符合契约即可。

## Evidence to gather (in priority order)
1. **Manifest / package metadata** — the strongest signal for the library's
   ecosystem. Look for:
   - `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg` → Python
   - `pom.xml`, `build.gradle*` → Java
   - `package.json` → Node.js
   - `Cargo.toml` → Rust
   - `go.mod` → Go
   - `*.csproj`, `*.fsproj` → .NET
2. **README / docs** — `README*`, `docs/`, project website links, the package
   description in `package.json` / `pyproject.toml` / `pom.xml`. This is the
   authors' own framing; weight it heavily but verify against code.
3. **Public API surface** — exported symbols: Python `__all__` and top-level
   `def`/`class` in package `__init__.py`; C/C++ public headers (`include/`);
   Java public classes; JS package `main`/`exports`. The public API reveals the
   intended capabilities better than internal files. When codegraph is available
   (the agent will tell you), use `codegraph context "<area>" -p repos/<name>` and
   `codegraph files -p repos/<name>` to map the symbol/module surface fast; fall
   back to grep/Read when it isn't.
4. **Module / directory layout** — top-level dirs often map to feature areas.
   借 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 看结构。
5. **A few key implementation files** — open the largest or most central
   production files to confirm what the API actually does.

**描述库本体（生产代码），不要把测试/示例当成库的能力。** 当一个仓库其实是**示例/教程
集合**（无可安装包；顶层目录基本都是按功能命名、各自独立可运行的 demo——如 PyQt 的
`QLabel/`/`QThread/`/`QAxWidget/`，外加 `Demo/`/`Test/`），如实说明它是「示例/教程集合，
非可发布生产库」，能力分类围绕「它演示了什么」而非把每个 demo 的平台用法当作库的特性。

## Determine the ecosystem
Before classifying capabilities, decide which ecosystem the library belongs to.
Use the manifest signal first; if ambiguous, fall back to the primary language
from the code-metrics output. Allowed values are exactly:

| Value    | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `python` | Python package (pip / poetry / setuptools) |
| `java`   | Java library / JAR (Maven / Gradle) |
| `nodejs` | Node.js / JavaScript package (npm / yarn / pnpm) |
| `cpp`    | C or C++ library |
| `rust`   | Rust crate |
| `go`     | Go module |
| `dotnet` | .NET library (C# / F#) |
| `other`  | Unclear or none of the above |

Rules:
- If multiple manifests exist, prefer the one that declares the primary package.
- If the repo is a polyglot binding wrapper (e.g. a Python package wrapping a C
  extension), classify by the package's distribution language/ecosystem.
- If no manifest is present and the primary language is mixed or unclear, use
  `other`.

## How to classify
- Group capabilities into **3–7 categories**, each a coherent feature area
  (e.g. "HTTP client", "Connection pooling", "TLS/SSL", "Async I/O").
- Each category needs concrete **evidence**: the file(s), module(s) or symbol(s)
  that implement it. No evidence → don't claim it.
- Identify the **domain** (networking / graphics / ML / crypto / data / GUI / …)
  and the **target users** (app developers? other libraries? CLI users?).

## Output (fills report `function_summary`)
```json
{
  "summary": "2-4 sentences: what it does and for whom.",
  "categories": [
    {"name": "...", "description": "...", "evidence": ["src/http/client.py", "Session"]}
  ],
  "domain": "networking",
  "target_users": "Python application developers",
  "ecosystem": "python"
}
```
Also set `library.one_liner` (<=120 chars), `library.ecosystem` (the **core**
ecosystem, one of the allowed values above), and `library.package_name` — the
**distribution/package name** declared in the manifest (`[project].name` / `name`
in `package.json` / Maven `artifactId` / `Cargo.toml` `name`), which may differ
from the repo dir name. Set it to `null` if there is no manifest or it is uncertain.
当**包名≠导入名或有别名/旧名**时，再填 `library.aliases`（其它已知名/旧名/CMake `find_package` 名/
Maven `groupId:artifactId`）与 `library.import_names`（实际 import 名，如 Pillow→PIL）——这些让本库
被别的库的依赖按名关联上（与 `package_name`/`source_url` 一起构成本库的身份键）。无则省略或 `[]`。

Set `library.bindings` — the languages the library exposes **bindings/wrappers**
for beyond its core ecosystem (so a polyglot library isn't shown as single-language).
E.g. a C++ core with Boost.Python + SWIG Java/C# bindings → `["python","java","dotnet"]`;
a JS package with a WASM/native core → list accordingly. Look for binding dirs/tools
(`*.pyx`/`pybind11`/Boost.Python, `*.i` SWIG, JNI `*Wrappers`, N-API, emscripten/CFFI).
Use `[]` if it only targets its core ecosystem.

## Language
- Write `summary`, every category `name`/`description`, `domain`, `target_users`,
  and `library.one_liner` in **简体中文 (Simplified Chinese)**. Keep proper nouns
  (library/API/dependency names, language names) in their original form.

## Rules
- Ground every claim in something you actually read. Never invent features.
- If docs and code disagree, trust the code and note it.
- If the library is large, sample breadth over depth — cover all top-level areas
  rather than fully reading one.

# Skill: license-detect

# License detection (model-driven)

A fixed regex table can't cover every license, exception, or dual-licensing
arrangement — so reason about it. Read the actual license text and decide.

## 主旨与原则
**输出契约（下方 Output）是唯一硬约束。** 下面的清单与取值是**推荐起点，不是封闭清单** ——
遇到不匹配的场景（罕见许可、自定义条款、SPDX 表里没有的组合），尽力判断，必要时给出最贴近的
SPDX 表达式或 `NOASSERTION`，并把疑难写进 `meta.observations`。方法仅是参考思路，可按仓库调整。

## Where to look (gather all, then reconcile)
1. **License files** — `LICENSE*`, `COPYING*`, `COPYRIGHT*`, `NOTICE*`,
   `UNLICENSE`, `LICENSES/` dir (REUSE spec). Read the full text, not just the
   filename.
2. **Manifest declarations** — `license`/`license-expression` in `package.json`,
   `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `<licenses>` in `pom.xml`, gradle.
3. **Source-file headers** — SPDX tags (`SPDX-License-Identifier: ...`) and
   copyright/permission banners at the top of representative source files. These
   catch cases where the repo has no top-level LICENSE, or where vendored code
   differs from the project license.
4. **README** "License" section.

## How to decide
- Map the text to the correct **SPDX identifier** (e.g. `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`,
  `BSD-3-Clause`, `GPL-3.0-only`, `LGPL-2.1-or-later`, `MPL-2.0`, `ISC`,
  `Unlicense`, `BSL-1.0`). Use a full SPDX expression for combinations
  (`Apache-2.0 OR MIT`, `GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0`).
- Detect **dual / multi licensing** (set `is_dual_licensed`).
- Flag **copyleft** (GPL/AGPL/LGPL), **weak copyleft** (MPL/LGPL), and any
  **exceptions** in `notes`, since these drive compliance obligations.
- If there is no license, an ambiguous one, or conflicting signals, set
  `spdx: "NOASSERTION"` (or `null`) and explain in `notes`.
- **归类协议性质到闭轴 `category`（5 选 1，见下表）** —— 与 spdx 判定并行给出。

### `category` — 协议性质（严格闭轴，只能映射不能新增）
把协议映射到**恰好一个**下列值（英文 key）：

| category | 含义 | 常见许可 |
|---|---|---|
| `strong_copyleft` | 强传染（整体传染） | GPL-2.0/3.0（含 -only/-or-later）、AGPL-3.0、EUPL、OSL |
| `weak_copyleft` | 弱传染（文件/库级） | LGPL-2.1/3.0、MPL-1.1/2.0、EPL-1.0/2.0、CDDL、CPL、Ms-RL |
| `permissive` | 友好（宽松） | MIT、BSD-2/3/4-Clause、Apache-2.0、ISC、Zlib、BSL-1.0、Unlicense、0BSD、CC0、Python-2.0 |
| `commercial` | 商业/源码可见非自由 | 专有/商业 EULA、保留所有权利、SSPL、BUSL-1.1、Elastic-2.0、Commons-Clause |
| `undeclared` | 未声明/无法判定 | 无 LICENSE、`null`、`NOASSERTION`、证据不足 |

- **双许可/多选一**（如 `GPL-2.0 OR MIT`）：按对使用者**最宽松**的那支归类（此例 → `permissive`），并在 `notes` 说明可选另一支。
- **WITH 例外**（如 `GPL-2.0 WITH Classpath-exception`）：仍按主许可家族归类（strong/weak），例外写 `notes`。

## Output (fills report `license`)
```json
{
  "spdx": "Apache-2.0",
  "name": "Apache License 2.0",
  "confidence": "high",
  "category": "permissive",
  "is_dual_licensed": false,
  "license_files": ["LICENSE"],
  "evidence": "LICENSE matches Apache-2.0 text; SPDX tag in src/*.cpp confirms.",
  "notes": "Permissive; requires NOTICE preservation."
}
```

## Rules
- Base `confidence` on evidence strength: `high` = unambiguous full license text;
  `medium` = manifest field or header tag only; `low` = inference.
- Note when vendored/third-party subtrees carry a different license than the project.
- **`category` 是严格闭轴的例外**：与本仓其它维度的"开放词表可扩"元规则**不同**，`category`
  **只能**是上表 5 个 key 之一——**禁止 coin 新值、禁止写入 `meta.observations`**。拿不准时选最贴近的一类
  （证据实在不足才用 `undeclared`）。`spdx`/`notes` 仍照常记录疑难。

## 自我发现（反哺）
遇到 SPDX 表难以覆盖的许可/例外/组合，或证据冲突的歧义，追加到顶层 `meta.observations`：

1: 		     README for GDB release
2: 
3: This is GDB, the GNU source-level debugger.
4: 
5: A summary of new features is in the file `gdb/NEWS'.
6: 
7: Check the GDB home page at http://www.gnu.org/software/gdb/ for up to
8: date release information, mailing list links and archives, etc.
9: 
10: GDB's bug tracking data base can be found at
11: http://www.gnu.org/software/gdb/bugs/
12: 
13: Unpacking and Installation -- quick overview
14: ==========================
15: 
16:    The release is provided as a gzipped tar file called
17: 'gdb-VERSION.tar.gz', where VERSION is the version of GDB.
18: 
19:    The GDB debugger sources, the generic GNU include
20: files, the BFD ("Binary File Descriptor") library, the readline
21: library, and other libraries all have directories of their own
22: underneath the gdb-VERSION directory.  The idea is that a variety of GNU
23: tools can share a common copy of these things.  Be aware of variation
24: over time--for example don't try to build GDB with a copy of bfd from
25: a release other than the GDB release (such as a binutils release),
26: especially if the releases are more than a few weeks apart.
27: Configuration scripts and makefiles exist to cruise up and down this
28: directory tree and automatically build all the pieces in the right
29: order.
30: 
31:    When you unpack the gdb-VERSION.tar.gz file, it will create a
32: source directory called `gdb-VERSION'.
33: 
34: You can build GDB right in the source directory:
35: 
36:       cd gdb-VERSION
37:       ./configure --prefix=/usr/local   (or wherever you want)
38:       make all install
39: 
40: However, we recommend that an empty directory be used instead.
41: This way you do not clutter your source tree with binary files
42: and will be able to create different builds with different
43: configuration options.
44: 
45: You can build GDB in any empty build directory:
46: 
47:       mkdir build
48:       cd build
49:       <full path to your sources>/gdb-VERSION/configure [etc...]
50:       make all install
51: 
52: (Building GDB with DJGPP tools for MS-DOS/MS-Windows is slightly
53: different; see the file gdb-VERSION/gdb/config/djgpp/README for details.)
54: 
55:    This will configure and build all the libraries as well as GDB.  If
56: `configure' can't determine your system type, specify one as its
57: argument, e.g., `./configure sun4' or `./configure decstation'.
58: 
59:    Make sure that your 'configure' line ends in 'gdb-VERSION/configure':
60: 
61:       /berman/migchain/source/gdb-VERSION/configure      # RIGHT
62:       /berman/migchain/source/gdb-VERSION/gdb/configure  # WRONG
63: 
64:    The GDB package contains several subdirectories, such as 'gdb',
65: 'bfd', and 'readline'.  If your 'configure' line ends in
66: 'gdb-VERSION/gdb/configure', then you are configuring only the gdb
67: subdirectory, not the whole GDB package.  This leads to build errors
68: such as:
69: 
70:       make: *** No rule to make target `../bfd/bfd.h', needed by `gdb.o'.  Stop.
71: 
72:    If you get other compiler errors during this stage, see the `Reporting
73: Bugs' section below; there are a few known problems.
74: 
75:    GDB's `configure' script has many options to enable or disable
76: different features or dependencies.  These options are not generally
77: known to the top-level `configure', so if you want to see a complete
78: list of options, invoke the subdirectory `configure', like:
79: 
80:       /berman/migchain/source/gdb-VERSION/gdb/configure --help
81: 
82:    (Take note of how this differs from the invocation used to actually
83: configure the build tree.)
84: 
85:    GDB requires a C++17 compiler.  If you do not have a
86: C++17 compiler for your system, you may be able to download and install
87: the GNU CC compiler.  It is available via anonymous FTP from the
88: directory `ftp://ftp.gnu.org/pub/gnu/gcc'.  GDB also requires an ISO
89: C standard library.  The GDB remote server, GDBserver, builds with some
90: non-ISO standard libraries - e.g. for Windows CE.
91: 
92:    GDB can optionally be built against various external libraries.
93: These dependencies are described below in the "`configure options"
94: section of this README.
95: 
96:    GDB can be used as a cross-debugger, running on a machine of one
97: type while debugging a program running on a machine of another type.
98: See below.
99: 
100: 
101: More Documentation
102: ******************
103: 
104:    All the documentation for GDB comes as part of the machine-readable
105: distribution.  The documentation is written in Texinfo format, which
106: is a documentation system that uses a single source file to produce
107: both on-line information and a printed manual.  You can use one of the
108: Info formatting commands to create the on-line version of the
109: documentation and TeX (or `texi2roff') to typeset the printed version.
110: 
111:    GDB includes an already formatted copy of the on-line Info version
112: of this manual in the `gdb/doc' subdirectory.  The main Info file is
113: `gdb-VERSION/gdb/doc/gdb.info', and it refers to subordinate files
114: matching `gdb.info*' in the same directory.  If necessary, you can
115: print out these files, or read them with any editor; but they are
116: easier to read using the `info' subsystem in GNU Emacs or the
117: standalone `info' program, available as part of the GNU Texinfo
118: distribution.
119: 
120:    If you want to format these Info files yourself, you need one of the
121: Info formatting programs, such as `texinfo-format-buffer' or
122: `makeinfo'.
123: 
124:    If you have `makeinfo' installed, and are in the top level GDB
125: source directory (`gdb-VERSION'), you can make the Info file by
126: typing:
127: 
128:       cd gdb/doc
129:       make info
130: 
131:    If you want to typeset and print copies of this manual, you need
132: TeX, a program to print its DVI output files, and `texinfo.tex', the
133: Texinfo definitions file.  This file is included in the GDB
134: distribution, in the directory `gdb-VERSION/texinfo'.
135: 
136:    TeX is a typesetting program; it does not print files directly, but
137: produces output files called DVI files.  To print a typeset document,
138: you need a program to print DVI files.  If your system has TeX
139: installed, chances are it has such a program.  The precise command to
140: use depends on your system; `lpr -d' is common; another (for PostScript
141: devices) is `dvips'.  The DVI print command may require a file name
142: without any extension or a `.dvi' extension.
143: 
144:    TeX also requires a macro definitions file called `texinfo.tex'.
145: This file tells TeX how to typeset a document written in Texinfo
146: format.  On its own, TeX cannot read, much less typeset a Texinfo file.
147:  `texinfo.tex' is distributed with GDB and is located in the
148: `gdb-VERSION/texinfo' directory.
149: 
150:    If you have TeX and a DVI printer program installed, you can typeset
151: and print this manual.  First switch to the `gdb' subdirectory of
152: the main source directory (for example, to `gdb-VERSION/gdb') and then type:
153: 
154:       make doc/gdb.dvi
155: 
156:    If you prefer to have the manual in PDF format, type this from the
157: `gdb/doc' subdirectory of the main source directory:
158: 
159:       make gdb.pdf
160: 
161: For this to work, you will need the PDFTeX package to be installed.
162: 
163: 
164: Installing GDB
165: **************
166: 
167:    GDB comes with a `configure' script that automates the process of
168: preparing GDB for installation; you can then use `make' to build the
169: `gdb' program.
170: 
171:    The GDB distribution includes all the source code you need for GDB in
172: a single directory.  That directory contains:
173: 
174: `gdb-VERSION/{COPYING,COPYING.LIB}'
175:      Standard GNU license files.  Please read them.
176: 
177: `gdb-VERSION/bfd'
178:      source for the Binary File Descriptor library
179: 
180: `gdb-VERSION/config*'
181:      script for configuring GDB, along with other support files
182: 
183: `gdb-VERSION/gdb'
184:      the source specific to GDB itself
185: 
186: `gdb-VERSION/include'
187:      GNU include files
188: 
189: `gdb-VERSION/libiberty'
190:      source for the `-liberty' free software library
191: 
192: `gdb-VERSION/opcodes'
193:      source for the library of opcode tables and disassemblers
194: 
195: `gdb-VERSION/readline'
196:      source for the GNU command-line interface
197:      NOTE:  The readline library is compiled for use by GDB, but will
198:      not be installed on your system when "make install" is issued.
199: 
200: `gdb-VERSION/sim'
201:      source for some simulators (ARM, D10V, SPARC, M32R, MIPS, PPC, V850, etc)
202: 
203: `gdb-VERSION/texinfo'
204:      The `texinfo.tex' file, which you need in order to make a printed
205:      manual using TeX.
206: 
207: `gdb-VERSION/etc'
208:      Coding standards, useful files for editing GDB, and other
209:      miscellanea.
210: 
211:    Note: the following instructions are for building GDB on Unix or
212: Unix-like systems.  Instructions for building with DJGPP for
213: MS-DOS/MS-Windows are in the file gdb/config/djgpp/README.
214: 
215:    The simplest way to configure and build GDB is to run `configure'
216: from the `gdb-VERSION' directory.
217: 
218:    First switch to the `gdb-VERSION' source directory if you are
219: not already in it; then run `configure'.
220: 
221:    For example:
222: 
223:       cd gdb-VERSION
224:       ./configure
225:       make
226: 
227:    Running `configure' followed by `make' builds the `bfd',
228: `readline', `mmalloc', and `libiberty' libraries, then `gdb' itself.
229: The configured source files, and the binaries, are left in the
230: corresponding source directories.
231: 
232:    `configure' is a Bourne-shell (`/bin/sh') script; if your system
233: does not recognize this automatically when you run a different shell,
234: you may need to run `sh' on it explicitly:
235: 
236:       sh configure
237: 
238:    If you run `configure' from a directory that contains source
239: directories for multiple libraries or programs, `configure' creates
240: configuration files for every directory level underneath (unless
241: you tell it not to, with the `--norecursion' option).
242: 
243:    You can install `gdb' anywhere; it has no hardwired paths. However,
244: you should make sure that the shell on your path (named by the `SHELL'
245: environment variable) is publicly readable.  Remember that GDB uses the
246: shell to start your program--some systems refuse to let GDB debug child
247: processes whose programs are not readable.
248: 
249: 
250: Compiling GDB in another directory
251: ==================================
252: 
253:    If you want to run GDB versions for several host or target machines,
254: you need a different `gdb' compiled for each combination of host and
255: target.  `configure' is designed to make this easy by allowing you to
256: generate each configuration in a separate subdirectory, rather than in
257: the source directory.  If your `make' program handles the `VPATH'
258: feature correctly (GNU `make' and SunOS 'make' are two that should),
259: running `make' in each of these directories builds the `gdb' program
260: specified there.
261: 
262:    To build `gdb' in a separate directory, run `configure' with the
263: `--srcdir' option to specify where to find the source. (You also need
264: to specify a path to find `configure' itself from your working
265: directory.  If the path to `configure' would be the same as the
266: argument to `--srcdir', you can leave out the `--srcdir' option; it
267: will be assumed.)
268: 
269:    For example, you can build GDB in a separate
270: directory for a Sun 4 like this:
271: 
272:      cd gdb-VERSION
273:      mkdir ../gdb-sun4
274:      cd ../gdb-sun4
275:      ../gdb-VERSION/configure
276:      make
277: 
278:    When `configure' builds a configuration using a remote source
279: directory, it creates a tree for the binaries with the same structure
280: (and using the same names) as the tree under the source directory.  In
281: the example, you'd find the Sun 4 library `libiberty.a' in the
282: directory `gdb-sun4/libiberty', and GDB itself in `gdb-sun4/gdb'.
283: 
284:    One popular reason to build several GDB configurations in separate
285: directories is to configure GDB for cross-compiling (where GDB runs on
286: one machine--the host--while debugging programs that run on another
287: machine--the target).  You specify a cross-debugging target by giving
288: the `--target=TARGET' option to `configure'.
289: 
290:    When you run `make' to build a program or library, you must run it
291: in a configured directory--whatever directory you were in when you
292: called `configure' (or one of its subdirectories).
293: 
294:    The `Makefile' that `configure' generates in each source directory
295: also runs recursively.  If you type `make' in a source directory such
296: as `gdb-VERSION' (or in a separate configured directory configured with
297: `--srcdir=PATH/gdb-VERSION'), you will build all the required libraries,
298: and then build GDB.
299: 
300:    When you have multiple hosts or targets configured in separate
301: directories, you can run `make' on them in parallel (for example, if
302: they are NFS-mounted on each of the hosts); they will not interfere
303: with each other.
304: 
305: 
306: Specifying names for hosts and targets
307: ======================================
308: 
309:    The specifications used for hosts and targets in the `configure'
310: script are based on a three-part naming scheme, but some short
311: predefined aliases are also supported.  The full naming scheme encodes
312: three pieces of information in the following pattern:
313: 
314:      ARCHITECTURE-VENDOR-OS
315: 
316:    For example, you can use the alias `sun4' as a HOST argument or in a
317: `--target=TARGET' option.  The equivalent full name is
318: `sparc-sun-sunos4'.
319: 
320:    The `configure' script accompanying GDB does not provide any query
321: facility to list all supported host and target names or aliases.
322: `configure' calls the Bourne shell script `config.sub' to map
323: abbreviations to full names; you can read the script, if you wish, or
324: you can use it to test your guesses on abbreviations--for example:
325: 
326:      % sh config.sub sun4
327:      sparc-sun-sunos4.1.1
328:      % sh config.sub sun3
329:      m68k-sun-sunos4.1.1
330:      % sh config.sub decstation
331:      mips-dec-ultrix4.2
332:      % sh config.sub hp300bsd
333:      m68k-hp-bsd
334:      % sh config.sub i386v
335:      i386-pc-sysv
336:      % sh config.sub i786v
337:      Invalid configuration `i786v': machine `i786v' not recognized
338: 
339: `config.sub' is also distributed in the GDB source directory.
340: 
341: 
342: `configure' options
343: ===================
344: 
345:    Here is a summary of the `configure' options and arguments that are
346: most often useful for building GDB.  `configure' also has several other
347: options not listed here.  There are many options to gdb's `configure'
348: script, some of which are only useful in special situation.
349: *note : (autoconf.info)Running configure scripts, for a full
350: explanation of `configure'.
351: 
352:      configure [--help]
353:                [--prefix=DIR]
354:                [--srcdir=PATH]
355:                [--target=TARGET]
356: 	       [--host=HOST]
357: 
358: You may introduce options with a single `-' rather than `--' if you
359: prefer; but you may abbreviate option names if you use `--'.  Some
360: more obscure GDB `configure' options are not listed here.
361: 
362: `--help'
363:      Display a quick summary of how to invoke `configure'.
364: 
365: `-prefix=DIR'
366:      Configure the source to install programs and files under directory
367:      `DIR'.
368: 
369: `--srcdir=PATH'
370:      *Warning: using this option requires GNU `make', or another `make'
371:      that compatibly implements the `VPATH' feature.*
372:      Use this option to make configurations in directories separate
373:      from the GDB source directories.  Among other things, you can use
374:      this to build (or maintain) several configurations simultaneously,
375:      in separate directories.  `configure' writes configuration
376:      specific files in the current directory, but arranges for them to
377:      use the source in the directory PATH.  `configure' will create
378:      directories under the working directory in parallel to the source
379:      directories below PATH.
380: 
381: `--host=HOST'
382:      Configure GDB to run on the specified HOST.  If you omit this,
383:      GDB will guess; it's quite accurate.
384: 
385:      The guess is done by running the `config.guess' script, which can
386:      be found in the root of the binutils-gdb source tree.
387: 
388:      There is no convenient way to generate a list of all available
389:      hosts.
390: 
391: `--target=TARGET'
392:      Configure GDB for cross-debugging programs running on the
393:      specified TARGET.  One way in which GDB supports cross-debugging
394:      is through the 'target remote' and 'target extended-remote'
395:      commands for remote debugging.  See the 'Remote debugging'
396:      section below.
397: 
398:      If this option is not specified, the default is the value of
399:      HOST, see `--host' above.
400: 
401:      When TARGET matches HOST, GDB will be configured with support for
402:      native debugging of programs running on the same machine as GDB.
403: 
404:      When TARGET and HOST are different, GDB will only include support
405:      for cross-debugging programs running on TARGET.
406: 
407:      There is no convenient way to generate a list of all available
408:      targets.
409: 
410: `--enable-targets=TARGET,TARGET,...'
411: `--enable-targets=all`
412:      Configure GDB for cross-debugging programs running on the
413:      specified list of targets in addition to the target specified
414:      with `--target' (see above).  The special value `all' configures
415:      GDB for debugging programs running on any target it supports.
416: 
417:      There is no convenient way to generate a list of all available
418:      targets.
419: 
420: `--enable-binary-file-formats=FORMAT,FORMAT,...'
421: `--enable-binary-file-formats=all'
422:     Configure GDB to only be be able to read selected file formats.
423:     The special value "all" causes all file formats to be compiled
424:     in, and is the default behavior of the option.  This option
425:     is meant for advanced users who are sure of what they expect,
426:     if you are unsure which options you will need on your debugging
427:     sessions, we recommend that you not use this feature.  The
428:     accepted options are:
429:       * coff: Main format on Windows systems, this is required to
430:         compile with windows target support;
431:       * dbx (also known as a.out): Legacy file format, this is
432:         recommended if you know you will be dealing with this
433:         file format;
434:       * elf: Main format on Linux systems, this is heavily
435:         recommended when compiling with linux support;
436:       * macho: Main format on MacOS systems, this is heavily
437:         recommended when compiling for those targets;
438:       * mips (also known as ecoff): Main file format for targets
439:         running on MIPS CPUs, this is heavily recommended when
440:         supporting those targets;
441:       * xcoff: Main format on AIX systems, this is required to
442:         compile for AIX targets and rs6000 CPUs.
443: 
444: `--with-gdb-datadir=PATH'
445:      Set the GDB-specific data directory.  GDB will look here for
446:      certain supporting files or scripts.  This defaults to the `gdb'
447:      subdirectory of `datadir' (which can be set using `--datadir').
448: 
449: `--with-relocated-sources=DIR'
450:      Sets up the default source path substitution rule so that
451:      directory names recorded in debug information will be
452:      automatically adjusted for any directory under DIR.  DIR should
453:      be a subdirectory of GDB's configured prefix, the one mentioned
454:      in the `--prefix' or `--exec-prefix' options to configure.  This
455:      option is useful if GDB is supposed to be moved to a different
456:      place after it is built.
457: 
458: `--enable-64-bit-bfd'
459:      Enable 64-bit support in BFD on 32-bit hosts.
460: 
461: `--disable-gdbmi'
462:      Build GDB without the GDB/MI machine interface.
463: 
464: `--enable-tui'
465:      Build GDB with the text-mode full-screen user interface (TUI).
466:      Requires a curses library (ncurses and cursesX are also
467:      supported).
468: 
469: `--disable-gdb-compile'
470:     Build GDB without support for the 'compile' command. DWARF support
471:     is required for this feature.
472: 
473: `--disable-gdb-dwarf-support'
474:     Build GDB without support for reading DWARF debug information.
475: 
476: `--disable-gdb-mdebug-support'
477:     Build GDB without support for reading mdebug debug information.
478: 
479: `--with-curses'
480:      Use the curses library instead of the termcap library, for
481:      text-mode terminal operations.
482: 
483: `--with-debuginfod'
484:      Build GDB with libdebuginfod, the debuginfod client library.  Used
485:      to automatically fetch source files and separate debug files from
486:      debuginfod servers using the associated executable's build ID.
487:      Enabled by default if libdebuginfod is installed and found at
488:      configure time.  debuginfod is packaged with elfutils, starting
489:      with version 0.178.  You can get the latest version from
490:      'https://sourceware.org/elfutils/'.
491: 
492: `--with-libunwind-ia64'
493:      Use the libunwind library for unwinding function call stack on ia64
494:      target platforms.
495:      See http://www.nongnu.org/libunwind/index.html for details.
496: 
497: `--with-system-readline'
498:      Use the readline library installed on the host, rather than the
499:      library supplied as part of GDB.  Readline 7 or newer is required;
500:      this is enforced by the build system.
501: 
502: `--with-system-zlib'
503:      Use the zlib library installed on the host, rather than the
504:      library supplied as part of GDB.
505: 
506: `--with-expat'
507:      Build GDB with Expat, a library for XML parsing.  (Done by
508:      default if libexpat is installed and found at configure time.)
509:      This library is used to read XML files supplied with GDB.  If it
510:      is unavailable, some features, such as remote protocol memory
511:      maps, target descriptions, and shared library lists, that are
512:      based on XML files, will not be available in GDB.  If your host
513:      does not have libexpat installed, you can get the latest version
514:      from `http://expat.sourceforge.net'.
515: 
516: `--with-libiconv-prefix[=DIR]'
517:      Build GDB with GNU libiconv, a character set encoding conversion
518:      library.  This is not done by default, as on GNU systems the
519:      `iconv' that is built in to the C library is sufficient.  If your
520:      host does not have a working `iconv', you can get the latest
521:      version of GNU iconv from `https://www.gnu.org/software/libiconv/'.
522: 
523:      GDB's build system also supports building GNU libiconv as part of
524:      the overall build.  See the GDB manual instructions on how to do
525:      this.
526: 
527: `--with-lzma'
528:      Build GDB with LZMA, a compression library.  (Done by default if
529:      liblzma is installed and found at configure time.)  LZMA is used
530:      by GDB's "mini debuginfo" feature, which is only useful on
531:      platforms using the ELF object file format.  If your host does
532:      not have liblzma installed, you can get the latest version from
533:      `https://tukaani.org/xz/'.
534: 
535: `--with-gmp=DIR'
536: `--with-gmp-lib=LIBDIR'
537: `--with-gmp-include=INCDIR'
538:      Build GDB using the GMP library installed at the directory DIR.
539:      If your host does not have GMP installed, you can get the latest
540:      version at `https://gmplib.org/'.
541:      The `--with-gmp=gmpinstalldir` option is shorthand for
542:      `--with-gmp-lib=gmpinstalldir/lib` and
543:      `--with-gmp-include=gmpinstalldir/include`.
544: 
545: `--with-mpfr=DIR'
546: `--with-mpfr-lib=LIBDIR'
547: `--with-mpfr-include=INCDIR'
548:      Build GDB using GNU MPFR installed at the directory DIR,
549:      a library for multiple-precision floating-point computation
550:      with correct rounding.
551:      This library is used to emulate target floating-point arithmetic
552:      during expression evaluation when the target uses different
553:      floating-point formats than the host.
554:      If your host does not have GNU MPFR installed, you
555:      can get the latest version from `https://www.mpfr.org/'.
556: 
557:      The `--with-mpfr=mpfrinstalldir` option is shorthand for
558:      `--with-mpfr-lib=mpfrinstalldir/lib` and
559:      `--with-mpfr-include=mpfrinstalldir/include`.
560: 
561: `--with-python[=PYTHON]'
562:      Build GDB with Python scripting support.  (Done by default if
563:      libpython is present and found at configure time.)  Python makes
564:      GDB scripting much more powerful than the restricted CLI
565:      scripting language.  If your host does not have Python installed,
566:      you can find it on `http://www.python.org/download/'.  The oldest
567:      version of Python supported by GDB is 3.4.  The optional argument
568:      PYTHON is used to find the Python headers and libraries.  It can
569:      be either the name of a Python executable, or the name of the
570:      directory in which Python is installed.
571: 
572: `--with-guile[=GUILE]'
573:      Build GDB with GNU Guile scripting support.  (Done by default if
574:      libguile is present and found at configure time.)  If your host
575:      does not have Guile installed, you can find it at
576:      `https://www.gnu.org/software/guile/'.  The optional argument
577:      GUILE can be a version number, which will cause `configure' to
578:      try to use that version of Guile; or the file name of a
579:      `pkg-config' executable, which will be queried to find the
580:      information needed to compile and link against Guile.
581: 
582: `--enable-source-highlight'
583:      When printing source code, use source highlighting.  This requires
584:      libsource-highlight to be installed and is enabled by default
585:      if the library is found.
586: 
587: `--with-xxhash'
588:      Use libxxhash for hashing.  This has no user-visible effect but
589:      speeds up various GDB operations such as symbol loading.  Enabled
590:      by default if libxxhash is found.
591: 
592: `--with-amd-dbgapi=[auto,yes,no]'
593:      Whether to use the amd-dbgapi library to support local debugging of
594:      AMD GCN architecture GPUs.
595: 
596:      When explicitly requesting support for an AMD GCN architecture through
597:      `--enable-targets' or `--target', there is no need to use
598:      `--with-amd-dbgapi': `configure' will automatically look for the
599:      amd-dbgapi library and fail if not found.
600: 
601:      When using --enable-targets=all, support for the AMD GCN architecture will
602:      only be included if the amd-dbgapi is found.  `--with-amd-dbgapi=yes' can
603:      be used to make it a failure if the amd-dbgapi library is not found.
604:      `--with-amd-dbgapi=no' can be used to prevent looking for the amd-dbgapi
605:      library altogether.
606: 
607: `--without-included-regex'
608:      Don't use the regex library included with GDB (as part of the
609:      libiberty library).  This is the default on hosts with version 2
610:      of the GNU C library.
611: 
612: `--with-sysroot=DIR'
613:      Use DIR as the default system root directory for libraries whose
614:      file names begin with `/lib' or `/usr/lib'.  (The value of DIR
615:      can be modified at run time by using the "set sysroot" command.)
616:      If DIR is under the GDB configured prefix (set with `--prefix' or
617:      `--exec-prefix' options), the default system root will be
618:      automatically adjusted if and when GDB is moved to a different
619:      location.
620: 
621: `--with-system-gdbinit=FILE'
622:      Configure GDB to automatically load a system-wide init file.
623:      FILE should be an absolute file name.  If FILE is in a directory
624:      under the configured prefix, and GDB is moved to another location
625:      after being built, the location of the system-wide init file will
626:      be adjusted accordingly.
627: 
628: `--with-system-gdbinit-dir=DIR'
629:      Configure GDB to automatically load system-wide init files from
630:      a directory. Files with extensions `.gdb', `.py' (if Python
631:      support is enabled) and `.scm' (if Guile support is enabled) are
632:      supported.  DIR should be an absolute directory name.  If DIR is
633:      in a directory under the configured prefix, and GDB is moved to
634:      another location after being built, the location of the system-
635:      wide init directory will be adjusted accordingly.
636: 
637: `--enable-build-warnings'
638:      When building the GDB sources, ask the compiler to warn about any
639:      code which looks even vaguely suspicious.  It passes many
640:      different warning flags, depending on the exact version of the
641:      compiler you are using.
642: 
643: `--enable-werror'
644:      Treat compiler warnings as werrors.  It adds the -Werror flag to
645:      the compiler, which will fail the compilation if the compiler
646:      outputs any warning messages.
647: 
648: `--enable-ubsan'
649:      Enable the GCC undefined behavior sanitizer.  By default this is
650:      disabled in GDB releases, but enabled when building from git.
651:      The undefined behavior sanitizer checks for C++ undefined
652:      behavior.  It has a performance cost, so if you are looking at
653:      GDB's performance, you should disable it.
654: 
655: `--enable-unit-tests[=yes|no]'
656:      Enable (i.e., include) support for unit tests when compiling GDB
657:      and GDBServer.  Note that if this option is not passed, GDB will
658:      have selftests if it is a development build, and will *not* have
659:      selftests if it is a non-development build.
660: 
661: `configure' accepts other options, for compatibility with configuring
662: other GNU tools recursively.
663: 
664: 
665: Remote debugging
666: =================
667: 
668:    Remote debugging is when GDB runs on one machine type (see `--host'
669: above), while debugging applications running on a possibly different
670: machine using the 'target remote' or 'target extended-remote'
671: commands.  The `--target' and `--enable-targets' configure options
672: control which targets GDB can debug.  Remote debugging is one way in
673: which GDB can support cross-debugging.  GDB runs on a machine of type
674: HOST (see `--host' configure option) but can remote debug a machine of
675: type TARGET (see `--target' and `--enable-targets' configure options).
676: 
677:    The files m68k-stub.c, i386-stub.c, and sparc-stub.c are examples
678: of remote stubs to be used with remote.c.  They are designed to run
679: standalone on an m68k, i386, or SPARC cpu and communicate properly
680: with the remote.c stub over a serial line.
681: 
682:    The directory gdbserver/ contains `gdbserver', a program that
683: allows remote debugging for Unix applications.  GDBserver is only
684: supported for some native configurations.
685: 
686:    The file gdbserver/README includes further notes on GDBserver; in
687: particular, it explains how to build GDBserver for cross-debugging
688: (where GDBserver runs on the target machine, which is of a different
689: architecture than the host machine running GDB).
690: 
691: 
692: Reporting Bugs in GDB
693: =====================
694: 
695:    There are several ways of reporting bugs in GDB.  The preferred
696: method is to use the World Wide Web:
697: 
698:       http://www.gnu.org/software/gdb/bugs/
699: 
700: As an alternative, the bug report can be submitted, via e-mail, to the
701: address "bug-gdb@gnu.org".
702: 
703:    When submitting a bug, please include the GDB version number, and
704: how you configured it (e.g., "sun4" or "mach386 host,
705: i586-intel-synopsys target").  Since GDB supports so many
706: different configurations, it is important that you be precise about
707: this.  The simplest way to do this is to include the output from these
708: commands:
709: 
710:       % gdb --version
711:       % gdb --config
712: 
713:    For more information on how/whether to report bugs, see the
714: Reporting Bugs chapter of the GDB manual (gdb/doc/gdb.texinfo).
715: 
716: 
717: Graphical interface to GDB -- X Windows, MS Windows
718: ==========================
719: 
720:    Several graphical interfaces to GDB are available.  You should
721: check:
722: 
723: 	https://sourceware.org/gdb/wiki/GDB%20Front%20Ends
724: 
725: for an up-to-date list.
726: 
727:    Emacs users will very likely enjoy the Grand Unified Debugger mode;
728: try typing `M-x gdb RET'.
729: 
730: 
731: Writing Code for GDB
732: =====================
733: 
734:    There is information about writing code for GDB in the file
735: `CONTRIBUTE' and at the website:
736: 
737: 	http://www.gnu.org/software/gdb/
738: 
739: in particular in the wiki.
740: 
741:    If you are pondering writing anything but a short patch, especially
742: take note of the information about copyrights and copyright assignment.
743: It can take quite a while to get all the paperwork done, so
744: we encourage you to start that process as soon as you decide you are
745: planning to work on something, or at least well ahead of when you
746: think you will be ready to submit the patches.
747: 
748: 
749: GDB Testsuite
750: =============
751: 
752:    Included with the GDB distribution is a DejaGNU based testsuite
753: that can either be used to test your newly built GDB, or for
754: regression testing a GDB with local modifications.
755: 
756:    Running the testsuite requires the prior installation of DejaGNU,
757: which is generally available via ftp.  The directory
758: ftp://sources.redhat.com/pub/dejagnu/ will contain a recent snapshot.
759: Once DejaGNU is installed, you can run the tests in one of the
760: following ways:
761: 
762:   (1)	cd gdb-VERSION
763: 	make check-gdb
764: 
765: or
766: 
767:   (2)	cd gdb-VERSION/gdb
768: 	make check
769: 
770: or
771: 
772:   (3)	cd gdb-VERSION/gdb/testsuite
773: 	make site.exp	(builds the site specific file)
774: 	runtest -tool gdb GDB=../gdb    (or GDB=<somepath> as appropriate)
775: 
776: When using a `make'-based method, you can use the Makefile variable
777: `RUNTESTFLAGS' to pass flags to `runtest', e.g.:
778: 
779: 	make RUNTESTFLAGS=--directory=gdb.cp check
780: 
781: If you use GNU make, you can use its `-j' option to run the testsuite
782: in parallel.  This can greatly reduce the amount of time it takes for
783: the testsuite to run.  In this case, if you set `RUNTESTFLAGS' then,
784: by default, the tests will be run serially even under `-j'.  You can
785: override this and force a parallel run by setting the `make' variable
786: `FORCE_PARALLEL' to any non-empty value.  Note that the parallel `make
787: check' assumes that you want to run the entire testsuite, so it is not
788: compatible with some dejagnu options, like `--directory'.
789: 
790: The last method gives you slightly more control in case of problems
791: with building one or more test executables or if you are using the
792: testsuite `standalone', without it being part of the GDB source tree.
793: 
794: See the DejaGNU documentation for further details.
795: 
796: 
797: Copyright and License Notices
798: =============================
799: 
800: Most files maintained by the GDB Project contain a copyright notice
801: as well as a license notice, usually at the start of the file.
802: 
803: To reduce the length of copyright notices, consecutive years in the
804: copyright notice can be combined into a single range.  For instance,
805: the following list of copyright years...
806: 
807:     1986, 1988, 1989, 1991-1993, 1999, 2000, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011
808: 
809: ... is abbreviated into:
810: 
811:     1986, 1988-1989, 1991-1993, 1999-2000, 2007-2011
812: 
813: Every year of each range, inclusive, is a copyrightable year that
814: could be listed individually.
